In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8589):

>## What this PR does / why we need it:
>
>The karpenter-operator previously only began deleting Karpenter NodePools and NodeClaims when the HCP received its DeletionTimestamp. In the HostedCluster deletion sequence, the HCP is deleted much later than regular HyperShift NodePools — after CAPI Cluster deletion, AWS endpoint service cleanup, and other steps complete. This meant Karpenter nodes were torn down sequentially after regular CAPI nodes instead of in parallel.
>
>Watch the CAPI Cluster object on the management side and treat its DeletionTimestamp as an early deletion signal. The CAPI Cluster is deleted at the same point regular NodePools are deleted, so Karpenter cleanup now runs concurrently with CAPI machine teardown.
>
>The karpenter finalizer on the HCP is only removed once the HCP itself has a DeletionTimestamp, preserving the existing gate for HCP deletion.
>
>Assisted by cursor agent with claude 4.6 opus.
>
>## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
><!--
>(optional, use `fixes #<issue_number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)` format, where issue_number might be a GitHub issue, or a Jira story
>-->
>no-jira
>
>## Special notes for your reviewer:
>
>Alternatively, we could have the hcp deletion flow set a special hcp annotation for the karpenter-operator to consume, but I chose to go this route to reduce internal APIs. This will speed up deletion by a good amount on autonode enabled clusters (since we no longer wait until capi object is deleted to cleanup karpenter anymore), so I'm hoping this will also solve some teardown timeout flakes.
>

## Walkthrough

This pull request adds cluster-aware deletion coordination to the Karpenter operator. The controller now watches CAPI Cluster resources on the management cluster and uses their deletion state to inform reconciliation behavior. An RBAC rule grants the operator permission to read Cluster resources. A new `isClusterDeleting` helper checks whether the HostedControlPlane or its referenced CAPI Cluster is being deleted. Reconciliation was updated to call this helper and adjust finalizer removal timing—the Karpenter finalizer is now only removed when the HCP itself has a DeletionTimestamp. Comprehensive test coverage was added for deletion scenarios involving both HCP and CAPI Cluster deletion states.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant KarpenterController
  participant HostedControlPlane
  participant ManagementCluster as CAPI_Cluster
  participant GuestCluster as NodeClaims

  HostedControlPlane->>KarpenterController: Reconcile request (HCP or namespace)
  KarpenterController->>KarpenterController: isClusterDeleting(hcp)
  alt hcp.DeletionTimestamp set
    KarpenterController-->>KarpenterController: return true
  else hcp.Spec.InfraID set
    KarpenterController->>CAPI_Cluster: GET Cluster (infraID namespace/name)
    CAPI_Cluster-->>KarpenterController: Cluster object (may have DeletionTimestamp)
  end
  opt clusterDeleting == true
    KarpenterController->>GuestCluster: List NodePools / NodeClaims
    GuestCluster-->>KarpenterController: NodePools / NodeClaims
    KarpenterController->>GuestCluster: Delete or annotate NodeClaims
    GuestCluster-->>KarpenterController: deletion/annotation results
    alt HostedControlPlane.DeletionTimestamp set
      KarpenterController->>HostedControlPlane: remove Karpenter finalizer
    else
      KarpenterController-->>HostedControlPlane: keep finalizer (defer)
    end
  end
```

Here is the analysis report: # Test Failure Analysis Complete ## Job Information - **Prow Job**: pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-e2e-aws - **Build ID**: 2060037378885554176 - **Target**: e2e-aws - **PR**: #8589 (NO-JIRA: fix(karpenter): start node cleanup when CAPI Cluster is deleted) - **Failed Step**: `e2e-aws-create-management-cluster` (pre phase) ## Test Failure Analysis ### Error ``` operation error EC2: CreateVpcEndpoint, https response error StatusCode: 400, RequestID: a217fb8d-60de-4c92-9593-c389d8f22850, api error VpcEndpointLimitExceeded: The maximum number of VPC endpoints has been reached. ``` ### Summary The job failed during the **pre phase** at the `create-management-cluster` step, before any test code from PR #8589 was executed. The AWS account used by the CI system had exhausted its VPC endpoint quota. When the HyperShift CLI attempted to create a VPC S3 endpoint as part of management cluster infrastructure provisioning, the AWS EC2 API rejected the request with `VpcEndpointLimitExceeded`. The VPC, subnets, route tables, and internet gateway were all created successfully — the failure occurred specifically at the VPC endpoint creation step. This is an infrastructure quota issue **unrelated to the PR's code changes** (which modify Karpenter node cleanup logic).
Root Cause The root cause is **AWS VPC endpoint quota exhaustion** in the CI account's `us-east-1` region. The `create-management-cluster` step runs the `hypershift create cluster aws` command, which provisions AWS infrastructure including a VPC S3 endpoint (a gateway endpoint for private S3 access). The AWS account has a per-region limit on the number of VPC endpoints. At the time this job ran (2026-05-28T17:02:49Z), the limit was already reached — likely due to leaked VPC endpoints from previous CI job runs that were not properly cleaned up. The failure call chain is: 1. `cmd/cluster/aws.NewCreateCommand.func1` (create.go:540) 2. → infrastructure creation 3. → `CreateVpcEndpoint` API call 4. → AWS returns HTTP 400 with `VpcEndpointLimitExceeded` This is a transient CI infrastructure problem. The PR's code changes (Karpenter node cleanup on CAPI Cluster deletion) were never exercised — the failure occurred before the management cluster was even created, so no hosted cluster was provisioned and no e2e tests ran.
Recommendations 1. **Rerun the job** — This is a transient infrastructure issue. A retry (`/retest`) should succeed if VPC endpoints have been freed by other completed jobs. 2. **No code changes needed** — The failure is entirely in the AWS environment, not in the PR's code. The Karpenter cleanup changes in PR #8589 were never tested. 3. **If retries continue to fail**, escalate to the CI infrastructure / DPTP team to investigate VPC endpoint leaks in the `hypershift-aws` CI account. Leaked endpoints from failed jobs that did not clean up properly are the most common cause of quota exhaustion.
Evidence | Evidence | Detail | |----------|--------| | **Failed Step** | `e2e-aws-create-management-cluster` (pre phase, 22s duration) | | **Phase** | `pre` — failure occurred before any test code ran | | **AWS API Error** | `VpcEndpointLimitExceeded` — HTTP 400 from EC2 `CreateVpcEndpoint` | | **AWS Request ID** | `a217fb8d-60de-4c92-9593-c389d8f22850` | | **Region** | `us-east-1` (subnets created in us-east-1a/1b/1c) | | **VPC Created** | `vpc-0fc6084e4af2cfb9d` (VPC created successfully before endpoint failure) | | **Error Location** | `cmd/cluster/aws/create.go:540` | | **Step Duration** | 22 seconds (failed almost immediately after infrastructure provisioning began) | | **Post Phase** | Succeeded — cleanup and dump steps completed normally | | **JUnit Failures** | 2 of 33 testcases: `create-management-cluster` container and `pre phase` | | **PR Relevance** | None — PR #8589 modifies Karpenter node cleanup, which runs post-cluster-creation |
